cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A latent global object is observed only through one projection or sensor. Before claiming reconstruction, one writes the observation map explicitly and tests whether distinct latent states can produce the same observed projection; if so, additional views or structural constraints are required.
common_abstraction: global target contains more coordinates than one local projection
a reconstruction claim requires sufficiency or injectivity of the observation map
non-identifiability can be exposed by constructing two admissible latent states with the same observed projection but different target coordinates
source_to_target_mapping: latent global state -> full BSD data package including complex Taylor data, regulator/period, all local factors, torsion and Sha
single sensor projection -> fixed-p Selmer/Iwasawa or p-adic leading-term output
additional sensor/constraint -> determinant reciprocity, all-prime/local-global input, or an archimedean comparison theorem
shared_constraints: the target claim must specify exactly which coordinates are reconstructed
the observation/projection map must be defined on the same admissible object class
a noninjective projection cannot certify a unique richer target without extra structure
disanalogies: BSD invariants are arithmetic, p-adic, and archimedean objects rather than numerical sensor coordinates
ordinary inverse-problem reconstruction formulas do not transfer to arithmetic geometry
some arithmetic coordinates may be linked by deep theorems rather than independently variable
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before inventing a higher-rank BSD bridge, formalize the map from the full BSD target package to the exact fixed-p theorem output and run a projection-sufficiency falsifier; any missing coordinate becomes a named child obstruction rather than being hidden inside 'Iwasawa implies BSD'.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Write the exact arithmetic projection and either prove a target-specific injectivity/reconstruction theorem or exhibit a rigorously admissible distinction showing that the registered p-primary output leaves a global/complex coordinate uncontrolled. The analogy itself supplies no mathematical evidence.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Structural identifiability analogy used only to select the next falsifier; no inverse-problem theorem is imported into BSD.

analogy_scan_notes: Scanned rank-zero/rank-one BSD mechanisms, arbitrary-rank Selmer/Iwasawa structure, Selmer-complex determinant formalisms, local-global arithmetic, and generic reconstruction/identifiability patterns. Retained only the projection-sufficiency analogy because it exposes a concrete falsifier without pretending that a non-arithmetic reconstruction theorem transfers.
